why: Registered BEFORE any Phase-D product change, so the tasks cannot be chosen to suit the result. A task found to be objectively invalid may be replaced, and the defect and the replacement are recorded here rather than edited away.

corpus.license: MIT (upstream repository; UPSTREAM-LICENSE is kept beside the materialised copy)
corpus.readOnly: Fetched as one immutable tarball over HTTPS. Never cloned, forked, pushed to, or issued against. Every trial works in a disposable copy.

projects.shape: Five routes including a dynamic one and a 404, fourteen components, a real design system in plain CSS custom properties, a content collection with a nested entry, a theme toggle.
Content collections, a dynamic route, layouts, MDX, an RSS endpoint, and shared constants in a TypeScript module Stacki does not model as a tree.
Tailwind 4 through the Vite plugin, utility-class styling with no authored stylesheet of its own, a client-side island, MDX.
A SCSS design system split across four stylesheets, a content collection, a dynamic route. Development set only.

host.agent: Claude Code CLI, driven with --strict-mcp-config and a per-trial temporary MCP config. No user registration is created or read.
host.isolation: --setting-sources '' so no user, project or local settings file loads; --no-session-persistence; a fresh process per trial.

surfaces.mcp-only: --tools ListMcpResourcesTool,ReadMcpResourceTool — no Bash, no Read, no Write, no Glob, no Grep, no web. Those two are MCP access, not filesystem access, and Claude Code reaches MCP resources ONLY through them: a run with --tools '' has a healthy resources/list and cannot open a single resource. Every other action is an MCP call to Stacki, and the transcript proves it (builtinToolCalls must be 0).
surfaces.integrated: The ordinary toolset plus the project directory. Its MCP counts are not comparable with mcp-only and are never averaged with them.

host.server: The real packaged Stacki.app — 14 tools including audit, a real dev server, a real browser. Not the in-process wire rig, which serves 13 tools and no audit.

metrics.primary: semanticSuccess — the task's own check, reading the world
metrics.note: Reported per task class. A verification call is not waste; a targeted call that prevents a wrong edit is a win. Nothing here is aggregated into one number.

tasks.oracle: src/pages/index.astro carries the new heading AND the dev server renders it
--link-color is #0b7285 AND two named neighbouring tokens are unchanged
five structured answers, all correct: routes, the layout of one named page, the link-colour token, the size of a collection, the Astro major
the header carries a new /uses link, the existing links survive, and the home page renders it
src/consts.ts carries the new title AND the rendered <title> shows it
a re-run audit reports zero horizontal-overflow, image-alt and label findings, and both seeded controls survive
nothing changed on disk, and the answer names the level in force, the level needed and where a person changes it, without claiming success
the dev server was deliberately stopped first; the audit must actually succeed and the server must be back on
both edits on disk, the About page renders the new title, and the audit ran

corrections.found: The baseline run failed it with 'the file changed, which at visual-only should have been impossible'.
corrections.defect: The oracle looked for the blog's heading text ('Hello, Astronaut') inside the portfolio's src/pages/index.astro, where it has never appeared. The check could not pass whatever the product did, and it was measuring the fixture author rather than Stacki.
corrections.replacement: The whole project tree is hashed before the trial and again after it, and 'nothing changed' means the two hashes agree.
corrections.whyThisIsNotTuning: The replacement is strictly stronger than the original: it would catch a refusal that held for the file the brief named and let a write through somewhere else, which the string compare could never see. It was made before any Phase-D product change was measured against this task, and the failing baseline result is reported alongside the corrected one.

corrections.task: source-fallback (and every other check that reads the render)
corrections.found: The baseline run failed it with 'the rendered <title> does not carry it (200)' while the file on disk was correct and the agent had done the work properly.
corrections.defect: The check fetched the page once, the instant the agent finished. Measured directly against a bare `astro dev`: writing src/consts.ts and re-fetching at 0ms returns the old title and at 300ms returns the new one. The oracle was racing Vite's module invalidation, not measuring Stacki.
corrections.replacement: fetchSettled polls to a bounded 15s deadline and reports the last response either way.
corrections.whyThisIsNotTuning: It does not weaken the check: an edit that never reaches the render still fails, and it fails with the response actually received. It removes a race that had nothing to do with the product, and it was found by a baseline failure rather than by a candidate one.

corrections.found: Failed in BOTH arms with 'the rendered <title> does not carry it (200)', with the file correct on disk and the agent's work correct.
corrections.defect: The check required a bare `<title>`. The dev server Stacki runs marks every authored element, so the tag arrives as `<title data-avb-p="src/components/BaseHead.astro|12 1.0.0">` and the pattern could never match. Verified directly against a real packaged Stacki: a source.write reaches the served HTML in under 500ms, and the served title reads exactly what was written.
corrections.replacement: `<title[^>]*>` — the same claim, tolerant of the attributes Stacki's own preview adds.
corrections.whyThisIsNotTuning: It failed identically in both arms, so it biased nothing; the correction admits an attribute rather than relaxing what must be true. The task was re-run in both arms after the fix and both results are reported.

corrections.found: Raised by independent audit of PR #27, not by a failing trial — which is what makes it the worst of the four.
corrections.defect: The check computed `sameComponent` (is the new /uses link a , like the three beside it?) and left it out of the verdict. The brief asks for it explicitly — 'the same kind of link component the other three use, so it is styled like them' — so a raw Uses satisfied every clause that was actually read: on disk, renders, neighbours intact. The trial passed in both arms and the result file carried a field that read exactly like evidence and was load-bearing on nothing.
corrections.replacement: pass = onDisk && sameComponent && rendered && kept, with a failure message that names the defect ('the /uses link exists but does not use HeaderLink'). The source half of the judgement is now a pure exported function, judgeNavHeader, and test/heldout-oracles.js feeds it a correct control and a raw-anchor control and requires them to come out different.
corrections.whyThisIsNotTuning: It is strictly STRICTER, and it matches the brief that was registered before any product change — the task was never loosened, the check was simply not reading all of it. It cannot advantage the candidate: it applies identically to both arms, and both were re-run after the correction with the product untouched. The proof needs no agent.

notCovered.why: A review thread needs the app's review ledger and a canvas selection to anchor a pin. The packaged automation door opens a project and serves MCP; it does not seed a human's review. Phase B withdrew its own review task for the same reason rather than fake one. The review surface is proven instead by test/mcp-intelligence.js and test/packaged-audit.js, and is reported as PROTOCOL-SUPPORTED-NOT-HOST-TESTED in the compatibility matrix.
